comment: Keys accepted in /etc/wsl.conf, the per-distribution file INSIDE a distribution. Not to be confused with .wslconfig, the Windows-side file for the VM as a whole, which has its own table in wslconfig-keys.json. A key WSL does not recognise is silently ignored, which is why the lint exists: a misspelling looks exactly like a setting that did not take effect.

keys.desc: Mount the Windows drives under the automount root.
Where the Windows drives are mounted.
Mount options for the Windows drives, for example metadata,uid=1000.
keys.note: These are appended to WSL's own defaults rather than replacing them, and an option WSL does not accept makes the whole value fail rather than being skipped.

keys.desc: Let WSL write /etc/resolv.conf from the Windows DNS settings.
keys.note: With this off, /etc/resolv.conf is yours to maintain. A stale one here is a common cause of name resolution working on Windows and not inside the distribution, especially after joining or leaving a VPN.

keys.desc: The hostname inside the distribution, instead of the Windows machine name.
Allow running Windows executables from inside the distribution.
Put the Windows PATH on the end of the PATH inside the distribution.
keys.note: Turning this off is a common cause of a Windows tool suddenly not being found from inside the distribution.

keys.desc: The user a shell starts as.
keys.note: This is read at start-up and written back to the DefaultUid value in the Windows registry, so changing it here and changing it with wsl --manage --set-default-user do the same thing.

keys.desc: Run systemd as the init inside the distribution.
keys.note: A distribution built to assume systemd, which most current ones are, will behave oddly without it: services do not start, and anything using systemctl fails.

keys.desc: A command to run as root when the distribution starts.
keys.note: It runs before any user shell and its failure is not reported anywhere obvious, so a mistake here looks like the distribution simply not working.
